test_runs.scope: small synthetic rotation, administrator route, role-gate and indicator-evaluator tests only

validation_runs.command: .venv/bin/python -m py_compile src/facecheck/rotation_control.py src/facecheck/platform_api.py src/facecheck/platform_catalog.py scripts/evaluate_indicators.py tests/test_rotation_control.py tests/test_cloud_access.py tests/test_indicator_evaluation.py

checks: SQLite queue persists rotation plan, object state, retry and interruption recovery
verified target publication is followed by transactional SQLite pointer, manifest anchor and key metadata switch with an audit event
stale source references fail compare-and-swap without switching the task
worker restart verifies and reuses a deterministic target published before interruption
v1 migration re-encrypts data while v2 recipient rotation rewraps the envelope
configured feature cache is invalidated; unresolved source and backup artifacts block revocation
hidden staging entries and legacy rows without key_id fail closed
duplicate source key rotation plans are rejected
rotation plan endpoint accepts typed request and returns controlled validation errors
administrator-only rotation routes reject auditor access
indicator evaluator retains PARTIAL and states global old-key invalidation is unproven
limitations: rewrap changes the recipient envelope but does not replace exposed per-video key material; compromise requires full data re-encryption
v1 to v2 migration temporarily materializes plaintext in a restricted staging directory; forced termination can leave staging data
writer fencing, reader drain and external backup completeness are operator/deployment attestations, not cross-node enforcement
SQLite and object storage do not share an atomic transaction; deterministic target publication is a local saga recovery mechanism
no real KMS/HSM revocation or complete external backup and disaster-recovery inventory was exercised
scope_note: Small synthetic functional evidence only. It does not prove production key management, global revocation, scale, or 100 percent old-key invalidation. Formal recognition and throughput results are unchanged.
